raw_response:
I've been working this land for 20 years. I know what Quzhou winters and summers ask of you. My wife and I are the only two in the house, so I can't do anything too complicated. I'm 72 now — my back isn't what it was. I'll keep to the rotation I know: wheat in the ground by early October, pull it in June, maize goes straight in after.

**On wheat:** I'll buy improved seed from the county seed station, same variety I've used for the last few years — it's reliable. I spread base fertilizer before rotary tillage, then top-dress nitrogen at jointing. I water three times: winter water in November to protect roots from freeze, jointing water in April, and one more at grain filling if it's dry. I spray herbicide early and fungicide once at heading for powdery mildew. I've seen what happens when you skip that.

**On maize:** I go with the hybrid the village seed dealer carries — something like Zhengdan 958 or similar, it yields well here. After wheat harvest I do no-tillage, plant straight into the stubble to save my back and hold moisture. Summer rains help, but I'll pump the well twice at critical stages — once before planting, once at jointing if July is dry. I apply urea in two splits: at planting and big bell stage. Two pesticide runs: one for corn borer, one herbicide pass early on.

I won't try anything new this year. At my age, with just the two of us, steady and familiar is how you get through the season.
